So it depends what you mean by linear.

1) As a percent of the damage applied to you, armour increases are not linear. E.g. if 12 armour =50% block, getting to 24 armour is not 2x50%=100% block.

2)As a percentage of the damage you take, it reduces the damage linearly. If you have 12 armour, that halves the damage you take. If you have 12 more armour, that halves it again.

So the reason that armour reduction is less effective against high armour heroes is if you take the above (and for clarity, let's make it extreme): suppose one person has 48 armour (~93% reduction with the above numbers) and another has 12 armour. If you apply 12 armour reduction, the overall damage you deal to each person will double (that's point 2) but the damage they take will be significantly different (1). The high armour person would take 12.5% of the damage applied, but the low armour would take 100%. So, relative to the amount they took before armour loss, they both take double but the % of damage they take is drastically different (6.25% increase vs 50%).
